shots.title: S01 · Start the case
shots.caption: New case → Ransomware intrusion. The template sets TLP:RED, seeds three hypotheses (exposed service, bought credentials, phishing loader), eight starter cards and four tasks. The case is named after the CISA alert code; the analyst name is stamped on everything from here on.
marks: Case switcher: the imported Okta case is also here

shots.title: S02 · Pull the IOCs out of the advisory
shots.caption: Extract IOCs with the advisory's indicator tables pasted in: nine IP addresses, six SHA-256 hashes and five CVEs are recognised and typed automatically. "Pin selected to board" creates one indicator card each.

shots.title: S03 · Evidence inbox
shots.caption: The SHA-1 hashes wait in the evidence inbox. Drag a card onto the board or press Pin; the remaining two stay unpinned (they still count in the Audit tab under "Still in the inbox").
marks: Pin (or drag the card onto the board)

shots.title: S06 · Photos and custody
shots.caption: Photo cards: "+ Photo" in the inbox, Pin, then Upload image in the Inspector. The file name, its SHA-256, who added it and when are recorded under Chain of custody. Here the analyst's own attack-path diagram; the other photo is a capture of the CISA advisory page.
marks: Upload image (also: drop a file on the board, or paste a screenshot)
Chain of custody: file name, SHA-256, added by, added at

shots.title: S06 · Cards with images
shots.caption: Cards with pictures: the person card shows the uploaded placeholder (no photo on file), location cards carry map captures of the hosting regions found through RDAP, photo cards hold the advisory capture and the analyst diagram. Target and transfer cards print sector, region, impact, amount, from and to.

shots.title: S07 · Arrange and cluster
shots.caption: The board arranged: dated events and sources down the left, actor / victim / ransom / tooling next, then three clusters: Infrastructure (the nine IPs with the two location cards), Malware & exploited CVEs (hashes and CVEs), and the ATT&CK playbook. Clusters are created with "+ Cluster", renamed in the panel, moved by their label and resized from the corner; cards inside move with them.
marks: Cluster label: drag to move the group

shots.title: S08 · Thread the evidence
shots.caption: Threads: Connect (C) with a relation picked on the toolbar, or drag a card's pin onto another card. Relations used here: controls (affiliate → infrastructure), located at (IP → map), resolves to (soc.dll → its C2), alias of (two locker.dll builds), linked to, suspected. The thread editor records the evidence, confidence, direction, and can cut the thread.

shots.title: S09 · OSINT on the C2 IP
shots.caption: OSINT on the C2 address 88.119.167[.]239: reverse DNS and RDAP come back live (UAB Bacloud, Lithuania, AS61272); AbuseIPDB, Shodan, Censys, GreyNoise, VirusTotal and the rest open as launchers. "Pin as card" writes the findings into the indicator card.

shots.title: S09 · OSINT on a hash
shots.caption: The same workbench with the soc.dll SHA-256: hash lookups go to VirusTotal, MalwareBazaar, Hybrid Analysis and others. Services that refuse browser requests are marked "blocked" with an Open link.

shots.title: S09 · OSINT on a CVE
shots.caption: CVE-2024-40711 (Veeam Backup & Replication, exploited by SafePay per CISA): the NVD lookup returns the description and CVSS live; launchers go to CVE.org, CISA KEV, EPSS and vendor advisories. Pin as card keeps the NVD text with the CVE.

shots.title: S10 · Pivots
shots.caption: Pivots on the selected indicator open VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, Shodan, Censys, GreyNoise, urlscan and more in a new tab (the VirusTotal result for this IP is in the next picture: 14 of 92 vendors flag it). "Copy defanged" copies 88.119.167[.]239 for reports. "Analyse with Claude" asks for an assessment when the board runs inside the Claude app; elsewhere it says so.

shots.title: S11 · Grade and handle
shots.caption: Grading the C2 address: stamped Confirmed, source A1 (completely reliable, confirmed), collected and first/last seen dates (last seen Aug 2026, so the Audit tab will list it as stale), a per-card TLP:AMBER override on a TLP:RED case, two tasks with due dates (the first is already overdue) and a dated comment.

shots.title: S11 · Tasks and comments
shots.caption: Tasks with due dates and comments on the same card. Overdue tasks are flagged in the Audit tab.

shots.title: S12 · Actor library
shots.caption: Actor library. SafePay is not in it, so LockBit (the closest RaaS playbook: exposed services, valid accounts, remote services, encryption) is dropped in as a comparison. Drop in pins the actor plus a technique card per TTP, threaded together.

shots.title: S12 · Merge duplicates
shots.caption: Merge: LockBit's "Exploit Public-Facing Application" duplicates the technique already on the board. Select the duplicate, pick the card to keep under MERGE, press Merge: threads are re-pointed, tags / tasks / comments are unioned and the duplicate is removed (Ctrl+Z undoes it).

shots.title: S13 · Threads tab
shots.caption: Threads tab: suggested threads appear when two cards share a tag, indicator or handle (accept or dismiss each), a manual form pins a thread between any two cards, and every thread is listed with its relation and confidence.

shots.title: S14 · Cross-case search
shots.caption: Search covers every case: "okta" dims this board (nothing here matches) and lists the hits from the imported Okta vishing case under the search box so you can jump across.

shots.title: S14 · Reveal
shots.caption: Reveal (R) with the affiliate card selected: only its direct threads (infrastructure it controls, victims, tools) and second-degree neighbours stay lit.

shots.title: S15 · Timeline
shots.caption: Timeline (T): from first SafePay activity in August 2024 through the IOC window to the advisory on 20 October 2026 and the analyst captures of 9 November; undated cards sit on the shelf.

shots.title: S15 · Kill chain
shots.caption: Kill chain (K): the thirteen techniques from the advisory fall into their ATT&CK tactic lanes, Initial Access through Impact, with threaded evidence under each.

shots.title: S16 · Competing hypotheses
shots.caption: ACH with the template's hypotheses: affiliate through an exposed service, credential bought from a broker, phishing with a loader. CISA reports both exposed-service CVEs and stolen credentials, so the first two stay consistent and the phishing-loader hypothesis collects the inconsistencies.

shots.title: S17 · Audit
shots.caption: Audit tab: the hygiene backlog. Unconnected cards, indicators without a stamp, events without a date, threads without evidence, stale indicators (last seen beyond 30 days), cards without a source, open and overdue tasks, and what is still in the inbox. Click a row to jump to the card.

shots.title: S18 · Snapshots and log
shots.caption: Log tab: a named snapshot was saved, then a note was added and a CVE card deleted. Diff lists exactly what changed since the snapshot; Restore puts the board back. Below: playback rebuilds the board card by card in date order, and the append-only log records every action with time and analyst.

shots.title: S18 · Playback
shots.caption: Playback running: cards appear in chronological order so you can walk a reviewer through how the picture built up. Pause, scrub with the slider, or Exit.

shots.title: S19 · Judgement and sign-off
shots.caption: Notes tab: the key judgement with High confidence and the dissent (several IPs sit in CDN / GitHub / Google ranges and should not be blocklisted blindly). Setting the review state to Published records "Signed off by S. Murugan" with the time; it prints on the brief.

shots.title: S20 · Request for information
shots.caption: Request generator switched to Request for information, addressed to the Bacloud abuse desk, with the indicators ticked. Open letter renders a printable RFI (next picture) that lists them defanged with the case number, TLP and analyst.

shots.title: S21 · Present
shots.caption: Present (P): panels hidden, exhibit counter at the bottom, arrow keys step through the numbered exhibits. Esc returns to the board.

shots.title: S22 · STIX round trip
shots.caption: The exported STIX 2.1 bundle imported back through Import: indicators, vulnerabilities, attack patterns, threat actor, identities, locations, the transaction, notes, relationships and groupings all come back as a new case (laid out on a grid). The same path accepts bundles from MISP / OpenCTI / vendor feeds.
marks: New case created from the bundle

shots.title: S23 · Finished board
shots.caption: Inbox and Panel toggled off for a clean view of the finished board; zoom with the wheel or the − / + buttons, F to fit.

shots.title: S23 · Encrypted at rest
shots.caption: Encrypt saved cases with a passphrase (TLP:RED material should not sit in plain localStorage). The next visit asks for it before anything is shown.

shots.title: S23 · Mobile
shots.caption: On a phone the same case is a list; Board / List and Panel toggles sit in the top bar.
